$comment: Hand-assigned scope complexity per app, read from each guide's research text. Rubric (also on the Method page): Low = one or a few coarse scopes or key-level permissions, nothing scope-triggered; Medium = granular scopes you must pick, justify or keep in sync (plan-dependent scopes, re-consent on change), but no scope-specific provider review for typical agent use; High = a scope a typical agent needs is gated by provider review, verification, advanced access, protected-data levels or admin consent that only some scopes require; N/A = no connector path. An admin who must install the whole app regardless of scopes is customer approval, recorded under approval, and doesn't raise the level on its own.

google-workspace.why: Gmail and full-Drive scopes are restricted (verification plus a yearly CASA assessment); Sheets, Docs, Calendar and gmail.send are sensitive.

microsoft-365.why: Mail.Read, calendars, shared files and Teams chats need customer admin consent in practice; channel messages and transcripts always do.

slack.why: Channel history and files:read get enhanced Marketplace review, search is Marketplace or internal only, and admin.* scopes are rejected.

github.why: Fine-grained GitHub App permissions (Contents, Pull requests, Issues and more); organization permissions need an org owner to install. No provider review.

notion.why: Five capabilities (read, update and insert content, comments, user information) and no scope-specific review.

meta.why: Every permission used on assets of businesses without a role on your app needs Advanced Access through App Review.

salesforce.why: A handful of coarse scopes (api, refresh_token, openid); real access comes from the user's profile and field-level security. Review follows the distribution route, not scopes.

hubspot.why: Required, optional and conditionally required scopes; tier-dependent scopes can fail installs, and listing review checks that every scope is used.

pipedrive.why: Scopes are fixed at registration and accepted all at once; no scope-specific approval is documented.

attio.why: One scope set configured in the console and shared with API keys; no scope-triggered review is documented.

twenty.why: Likely no scope model: permissions follow the role assigned to the API key (unverified).

podio.why: Likely one coarse scope (for example global:all); access follows the user's Podio permissions (unverified).

zoho-crm.why: Fine-grained module and operation scopes (for example ZohoCRM.modules.contacts.READ); no scope review for direct OAuth use.

close.why: Likely coarse scopes (all.full_access, offline_access); behaviour follows the authorizing user's permissions (unverified).

copper.why: Likely no fine-grained scopes; access follows the authorizing user's Copper permissions (unverified).

dealcloud.why: Likely a small scope set; real permissions come from the service user's role in the tenant (unverified).

zendesk.why: Broad read/write or resource scopes such as tickets:read, and Zendesk may cap your client's allowed scopes when it approves you.

intercom.why: Scopes are picked in the Developer Hub; reviewers compare them with the app's features and may ask you to trim and resubmit.

freshdesk.why: No scopes: the key carries the creating user's role permissions.

front.why: Scopes are selected on the app and approved by customer admins at install (scope list not verified).

pylon.why: No scopes: permissions come from the token's role; older tokens without a role act as Admin.

liveagent.why: No scopes documented; the key likely inherits its owner's agent permissions.

plain.why: Permissions are chosen per key when it is created.

helpscout.why: No OAuth scopes documented; access likely follows the authorizing user's permissions.

gorgias.why: Many read/write scope pairs (tickets, customers, macros, rules…) to choose from; none documented as needing extra approval.

gladly.why: No scopes: a token can do anything its user can, so use a dedicated user.

twilio.why: No OAuth scopes; ask customers for a Restricted key limited to the resources you use.

zoho-cliq.why: Per-endpoint scopes (ZohoCliq.<Resource>.<READ|CREATE|UPDATE|DELETE>); no scope-level review documented.

lark.why: Granular per-API scopes; sensitive scopes need tenant admin approval at release, and store review likely scrutinizes them.

pumble.why: User scopes and bot scopes; no scope-level review documented.

discord.why: Common scopes are self-serve, but dm_channels.read, voice and rpc.* are approval-only and the message content intent is privileged.

telegram.why: No scope model for bots; capabilities come from bot settings and admin rights.

whatsapp-business.why: Both whatsapp_business_management and whatsapp_business_messaging need Advanced Access through App Review.

aircall.why: Only the public_api scope is documented.

vonage.why: No OAuth scopes; applications are limited by their enabled capabilities.

google-ads.why: One scope (adwords) covers read and write; Google reviews your developer-token access level, not scopes.

meta-ads.why: ads_read and ads_management need Advanced Access through App Review to serve other businesses.

linkedin-ads.why: Scopes (r_ads, rw_ads, r_ads_reporting…) come with each approved API product, and members also need the matching role.

gohighlevel.why: Scopes are selected per app and reviewers ask you to justify them.

mailchimp.why: No scope parameter; the token likely acts with the user's access to the whole account.

klaviyo.why: Klaviyo requires the least permissive scope set and rejects apps that request excess scopes in review.

systeme-io.why: No scopes known; a key presumably grants account-wide access.

pinterest.why: Read and write scopes per resource (boards, pins, ads); new apps can get 403s on boards or Pins without user authorization.

threads.why: Each Threads permission (publish, replies, insights) needs App Review before non-role users can grant it.

sendgrid.why: No OAuth; ask customers for a restricted key with mail.send and only the other permissions you use.

shopify.why: Customer data needs protected customer data Level 1, and name, email, phone or address need Level 2; both are checked at App Store review.

woocommerce.why: Only read, write or read_write per key; nothing triggers a review.

bigcommerce.why: Scopes are fixed in the app profile, merchants can't pick a subset, and changing scopes forces re-acceptance.

salesforce-commerce-cloud.why: Roles and scopes on the API client plus per-client resource permissions in Business Manager; SLAS clients carry their own scopes.

magento.why: The merchant ticks API resources in an ACL tree when creating the integration; no scope names or review triggers.

squarespace.why: A short list of website.* scopes with .read variants; no scope-specific review documented.

ecwid.why: Access scopes chosen in app settings (catalog, orders, customers…); exact names not confirmed.

gumroad.why: A few scopes (view_sales, edit_products, refund_sales…); refunds and edits are the sensitive ones, with no review known.

amazon-selling-partner.why: Roles that expose personal data need Restricted Data Tokens plus Data Protection Policy controls and approval.

dataforseo.why: No scopes: the credentials reach every API the funded balance pays for.

se-ranking.why: No scopes: keys have full account access.

ahrefs.why: A single scope; the constraints are in the data-storage terms, not in scopes.

mrscraper.why: No scopes documented; a token has the account's full API access.

apify.why: Tokens are account-level or resource-specific; OAuth scopes aren't documented.

firecrawl.why: No scopes: a key has the team's full API access.

bright-data.why: No OAuth scopes; permissions follow the user role and the key.

waterfall-io.why: No scopes documented; sub-keys partition access and usage.

clay.why: No scopes documented; access equals the key owner's workspace permissions.

vercel.why: A dozen integration scopes, each Read or Read/Write; adding or upgrading scopes needs confirmation from users or team owners.

netlify.why: No scope model documented; tokens appear to act with the user's full API access.

cloudflare.why: Scopes mirror API token permissions; you mark which are required or optional, and users choose read-only or full access.

supabase.why: Per-app Read/Write scopes set at creation; no scope triggers approval.

neo4j.why: No scopes: the token inherits its creator's roles.

snowflake.why: Tokens are pinned to a role (session:role:<name>); admin roles are blocked unless Snowflake Support changes it.

mongodb-atlas.why: Organization and project roles limit operations, and database data needs separate database users.

datadog.why: Request the minimum from Datadog's scopes reference; api_keys_write is needed to create the customer's API key.

sentry.why: Standard org-wide API permissions chosen on the integration and approved by users at install.

airtable.why: Granular scopes plus per-base selection by the user; no scope triggers review.

linear.why: read by default plus a few narrow write scopes; customer and initiative scopes are separate opt-ins.

jira.why: Granular and classic scopes added per API in the console; changing scopes forces re-consent and some resources aren't available to 3LO.

asana.why: resource:action scopes; endpoints without scopes need Full permissions, and opt_fields need matching scopes or return 403.

monday.why: Read and write scopes across many areas; requested scopes must match the app's configured scopes.

clickup.why: No scope parameter; the token acts with the user's permissions in the Workspaces they choose.

coda.why: No OAuth scopes; tokens follow the owner's access, optionally narrowed per doc or operation.

smartsheet.why: 17 scopes (ADMIN_, CREATE_, READ_, WRITE_ and more) that don't override sharing permissions.

harvest.why: Coarse scopes only: you choose products and accounts, not read or write.

stripe.why: Stripe Apps permissions are declared in the manifest, and each needs a written justification at review.

plaid.why: Access is per Plaid product, each enabled by a Production request; adding a product later needs another request.

binance.why: Per-key permission toggles (read, trading, withdrawals); the OAuth scope list wasn't available.

paygent-connect.why: Key permission types chosen when the key is created.

ipayx.why: No scope model documented; one token covers the API and MCP tools.

quickbooks.why: A few broad scopes (accounting, payment, OpenID); no read-only accounting scope is documented.

xero.why: Additive scopes across many products; journals, Practice Manager and bulk connections need a security assessment.

brex.why: Space-delimited scopes, and the granted set can be a subset of what you asked for.

ramp.why: resource:permission scopes; start read-only. cards:read_vault needs an extra security review.

pitchbook.why: No scope model confirmed; access follows the licence entitlement.

notebooklm.why: No connector path: IAM-based Cloud API, no OAuth scopes for third-party apps.

otter-ai.why: No connector path for third-party apps is documented.

fathom.why: One scope (public_api) with full API access for the authorizing user.

consensus.why: No connector path for third-party apps is documented.

reducto.why: Keys are all-or-nothing for the account.

devin.why: RBAC roles on the service user rather than OAuth scopes.

higgsfield.why: No scope model documented; keys are per project.

mermaid-cli.why: Local tool; no authentication or permissions apply.

youtube-transcript.why: The transcript API has no scopes (the official YouTube Data API's force-ssl scope is sensitive).

grain.why: Two scopes: personal (default) and workspace (admin- and plan-gated).
